speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; to help me understand your condition, please have your caregiver tell me exactly when these episodes occur, such as during crying, feeding, or sleeping. Also, has anyone noticed if the noise changes pitch or stops completely during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

The combination of inspiratory stridor worsening with neck flexion and crying, along with post-prandial vomiting, strongly points to this diagnosis. I will now request an Upper Airway Endoscopy to visualize the supraglottic structures and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Upper_Airway_Endoscopy
